extracted.intended_audience: Officials and staff of Federal agencies who prepare, file, or publish documents in the Federal Register and Code of Federal Regulations; legal publishers, librarians, and members of the public who use these publications.
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, policies, and procedural criteria for agencies and the Office of the Federal Register governing what documents must or may be filed and published, how documents are filed and made available to the public, and how the CFR is compiled, updated, indexed, and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document having general applicability and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Document having general applicability and legal effect means any document issued under proper authority prescribing a penalty or course of conduct, conferring a right, privilege, authority, or immunity, or imposing an obligation, and relevant or applicable to the general public, members of a class, or persons in a locality, as distinguished from named individuals or organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to determine which agency instruments qualify for filing and publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER and codification in the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing — when a document is considered filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing means making a document available for public inspection at the Office of the Federal Register during official business hours. A document is filed only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date according to the schedule in part 17 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not treat submission alone as filing; Office of the Federal Register's receipt+processing+publication-date assignment is required before a document is 'filed' for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to return documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may return to the issuing agency any document submitted for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER, or a special edition thereof, if in the Director’s judgment the document does not meet the minimum requirements of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure submissions meet formatting, content, and procedural minimums to avoid return; the Director administers the chapter generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy — required contents of the FEDERAL REGISTER
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall publish a serial publication called the FEDERAL REGISTER to contain: (1) Executive orders, proclamations, and other Presidential documents; (2) documents required to be published therein by law; and (3) documents accepted for publication under § 5.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FEDERAL REGISTER's scope is defined by statute and this policy; agencies must know which categories of materials are required or eligible for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt publication subject to accuracy, usability, and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document required or authorized to be filed for publication shall be published in the FEDERAL REGISTER as promptly as possible, within limitations imposed by considerations of accuracy, usability, and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is a goal but may be balanced against accuracy and cost; agencies should provide materials that permit prompt publication without sacrificing accuracy or usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required to be filed and published
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents are required to be filed for public inspection with the Office of the Federal Register and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER: (a) Presidential proclamations and Executive orders in the numbered series, and each other document that the President submits for publication or orders to be published; (b) each document or class of documents required to be published by act of Congress; (c) each document having general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify when statutes or the nature of a document impose a mandatory filing/publication obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may publish other documents in public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Director of the Federal Register considers that publication of a document not covered by § 5.2 would be in the public interest, the Director may allow that document to be filed for public inspection with the Office of the Federal Register and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary publications are possible but depend on Director determination of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication not authorized — exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 15 of title 44 does not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements, or proclamations thereof by the President. It prohibits the publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER of comments or news items. The Director may not accept documents unless they are the official action of the agency concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not submit treaties or informal materials (comments/news) for FEDERAL REGISTER publication; only official agency actions qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of documents for placement in the FEDERAL REGISTER
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document published in the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be placed under one of the following categories: (a) The President; (b) Rules and regulations (documents having general applicability and legal effect, including codified rules, policy statements, interpretations, organizational statements); (c) Proposed rules (notices of proposed rulemaking submitted pursuant to section 553 of title 5 or other law); (d) Notices (miscellaneous documents applicable to the public and not covered by the other paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper categorization affects filing, indexing, and users' ability to find documents; agencies must select the correct category according to content and legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of citation
rubrics_metrics.description: FEDERAL REGISTER material may be cited by volume and page number, and the short form 'FR' may be used for 'FEDERAL REGISTER' (e.g., '37 FR 6803').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard citation form for legal references and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily publication schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER published for each official Federal working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should time submissions to meet daily publication schedules; see part 17 for timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Printing Office shall distribute the FEDERAL REGISTER by delivery or by deposit at a post office at or before 9 a.m. on the publication day, except that each FEDERAL REGISTER dated for a Monday shall be deposited at a post office at or before 9 a.m. on the preceding Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution timing ensures public availability; agencies should be aware of GPO logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication (FEDERAL REGISTER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee publishes the FEDERAL REGISTER in the following formats: paper; microfiche; and online on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide materials suitable for multiple media; online availability is provided via GPO Access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of documents at Office of the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed with the Office of the Federal Register pursuant to law are available for public inspection at 800 North Capitol Street, NW., suite 700, Washington, DC, during the Office of the Federal Register office hours. There are no formal inspection procedures or requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public can inspect filed documents in person during office hours; agencies should ensure files are complete and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing timing and notation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall cause each document received by the office to be filed for public inspection not later than the working day preceding the publication day for that document. The Director shall cause to be placed on the original and certified copies of each document a notation of the day and hour when it was filed and made available for public inspection. Photocopies or excerpts may be made at the inspection desk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies can rely on these practices for establishing public filing dates and documenting availability; certified copies will carry timestamp notations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information services limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Information concerning the publications and original acts and documents filed with the Office of the Federal Register is provided by staff, but the staff may not summarize or interpret substantive text of any act or document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office can assist with reference and retrieval but will not provide substantive legal interpretation; agencies and users should seek agency legal interpretation for content questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and certification governed by National Archives regs
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations for the public use of records in the National Archives (36 CFR parts 1252–1258) govern the furnishing of reproductions of acts and documents and certificates of authentication for them. Section 1258.14 provides for advance payment of appropriate fees for reproduction services and for certifying reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for certified reproductions follow NARA fee and procedure rules; agencies and users should consult 36 CFR for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and ancillaries responsibilities (daily and cumulative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be appropriately indexed. Analytical subject indexes covering the contents shall be published as currently as practicable and cumulated and separately published at least once each calendar year. Each daily issue shall carry a numerical list of the parts of the CFR specifically affected by documents published in that issue and, beginning with the second issue of each month, shall carry a cumulated list of the parts affected during that month. A monthly list of sections of the CFR affected shall be separately published on a cumulative basis during each calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indexing and list products (including the monthly LSA) help users determine amendments and affected CFR sections; agencies should ensure their publications include correct citations to facilitate indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes, digests, and guides — special editions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order preparation and publication of indexes, digests, and similar guides based on laws, Presidential documents, regulatory documents, and notices, which will serve users. Each index, digest, and guide is considered a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER whenever public need requires special printing or special binding in substantial numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may coordinate with the Office to provide materials for ancillary guides; special editions are produced when public need justifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall publish periodically a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER to present a compact and practical code called the 'Code of Federal Regulations', to contain each Federal regulation of general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations meeting the 'general applicability and legal effect' definition are to be codified in the CFR; agencies must prepare codified text in the form suitable for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep CFR current and usable within dependability and cost limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee intends that every practical means be used to keep the Code as current and readily usable as possible, within limitations imposed by dependability and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should work to ensure submissions facilitate timely codification but recognize practical constraints of cost and production reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly development of CFR titles and rearrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure orderly development of the CFR, the Director may establish new titles and rearrange existing titles and subordinate assignments; before taking such action the Director shall consult with each agency directly affected by the proposed change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies impacted by structural changes will be consulted; plan for coordination if title changes are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR periodic updating and cutoff dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book of the Code shall be updated at least once each calendar year. If no change has occurred, a simple notation may serve as the supplement. More frequent updating may be made whenever the Director determines the content has been substantially superseded. The Code will be produced over a 12-month period under a staggered publication system. Each updated title will reflect each amendment to that title published on or before the 'As of' date (cutoff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should note the 'As of' cutoff dates for updated titles to know which amendments will be incorporated; request more frequent updating if content is substantively superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR indexes and agency-prepared indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject index to the entire Code shall be annually revised and separately published. An agency-prepared index for any individual book may be published with the approval of the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may prepare and propose their own book-level indexes, subject to Director approval, to assist users of specific CFR titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillaries for the CFR — parallel tables and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code shall provide finding aids including: (a) parallel tables of statutory authorities and rules (lists of U.S. Code sections cited as rulemaking authority arranged with parallel CFR citations); (b) parallel tables of Presidential documents and agency rules; (c) list of CFR sections affected (numerical list following each CFR volume identifying sections affected by FR documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ancillaries assist legal research and tracking of authority; agencies should include proper statutory and Presidential citations in rulemaking to support these tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — legal effect and approval criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference treats material as if published in full in the Federal Register (5 U.S.C. 552(a)). The Director will approve an incorporation by reference only when requirements of 1 CFR part 51 are met. Elements on which approval is based include: (a) The incorporation will substantially reduce the volume of material published in the Federal Register; (b) The matter incorporated is in fact available to the extent necessary to afford fairness and uniformity in the administrative process; (c) The incorporating document is drafted and submitted for publication in accordance with 1 CFR part 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference is permissible but requires Director approval and availability of the incorporated material; agencies must follow part 51 procedures and ensure public access to incorporated material. If incorporated material cannot be found, contact the issuing agency and then notify the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obsolete provisions not carried in current CFR volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that become obsolete before the revision date stated on the cover of each volume are not carried. Users may find past texts via the List of CFR Sections Affected (LSA) or past LSA volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and users seeking removed or prior provisions should consult LSA and historical LSA volumes for the relevant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB control numbers placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paperwork Reduction Act requires Federal agencies to display an OMB control number with their information collection request. These OMB numbers are placed as close as possible to the applicable recordkeeping or reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must include OMB control numbers adjacent to the requirements they authorize; many agencies publish these as amendments in the CFR.
